textbookText: Aristotle was a renowned ancient Greek philosopher who dedicated himself to unraveling life's mysteries, becoming the first genuine scientist in history. Aristotle's pioneering contributions spanned philosophy and science, where he introduced formal logic and delineated the relationships between various scientific disciplines. Aristotle's groundbreaking works include animals’ classification (in book "History of Animals"), binomial nomenclature. His profound impact on science endures, making him a revered figure in human history.
